content_preview.title: Zed Launches Delta in Public Beta, a Multiplayer Coding Environment Built to Replace GitHub Pull Requests
content_preview.summary: Zed Industries opened public beta access to Delta, a collaborative environment for coding with AI agents that the company says is meant to replace pull requests.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Zed Industries, the company behind the Zed code editor, opened public beta access to Delta on September 16, 2026, according to [Zed's official blog](https://zed.dev/blog/delta-public-beta). Delta is described in the announcement as "a multiplayer environment for coding with agents and reviewing what they build," and the company frames it as the start of an effort to move development work away from GitHub's pull-request model, as stated in [the announcement](https://zed.dev/blog/delt...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece with clear Overview / What We Know / Framing / What We Don't Know sections. Claims are consistently attributed inline to Zed's blog posts, and the article correctly distinguishes the September 16, 2026 public-beta announcement from the August 12, 2026 private-beta announcement (two separate posts, both cited appropriately by which post supports which claim).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots in full from sources/2026-09/zed-launches-delta-in-public-beta-a-multiplayer-coding-environment-built-to-replace-github-pull-requests/: source-0.html.gz (https://zed.dev/blog/delta-public-beta, 'Replace PRs with Delta - Now in Public Beta', dated September 16, 2026, sha256 7708d3b0...ba05bad2588 verified against manifest) and source-1.html.gz (https://zed.dev/blog/introducing-delta, 'Introducing Delta', dated August 12, 2026, sha256 3b1a4252...ce60804fa3a verified against manifest). Both returned HTTP 200 directly (no archive_fallback), manifest suspicious_patterns is null for both. Checked every direct quote in the article against the extracted snapshot text and confirmed each is verbatim, including: 'a multiplayer environment for coding with agents and reviewing what they build'; 'agents have fundamentally changed the way we write software, but our collaborative tooling isn't keeping up'; 'the diffs we're asking each other to review have mushroomed'; 'see the same worktrees'/'can work with them on their own machine'/'can keep working with the agent where you left off'; 'dedicated review subthread'/'its own isolated copy of the parent thread's worktrees'; the DeltaDB description ('extends Git's content-based versioning with incremental versions based on deltas', 'records edits between commits alongside messages from humans and agents', 'remains the checkpoint you push, pull, and build from'); 'connects to third-party agent harnesses, starting with Claude Code' (correctly attributed to the introducing-delta post, source-1); 'zed-industries/zed will remain on GitHub for now because it's where our community finds issues and submits changes'; 'share Delta threads alongside their pull requests'; 'Last week, we crossed a key milestone: we disabled pull requests on Delta's own repository'; '33 of us have landed 570 changes to main since we turned off pull requests'; 'introduce paid plans soon for individuals and teams'/'There will always be a free version of Delta'; 'pull requests are the first part of the GitHub workflow we're leaving behind'; 'continuous engineering'; 'it seems like everyone is in a race to replace GitHub right now'; 'the same old primitives: branches, commits, and diffs'; 'an agent can trigger a run with an existing CI provider and check the results before landing the change'. No hallucinated or misattributed quotes found. All non-quoted paraphrases (download availability across macOS/Linux/Windows/web/mobile, framing of the private-to-public beta timeline) are accurate summaries of the source text.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific claim in the article — the September 16, 2026 public beta date, the August 12, 2026 private beta date, the DeltaDB architecture description, the Claude Code integration, the '33 of us / 570 changes' internal-adoption figure, and the free-during-beta / paid-plans-coming pricing note — traces directly to the two cited Zed blog posts. The 'What We Don't Know' section is itself accurate: the source posts do not give a price or launch date for paid plans, and do not state whether/when zed-industries/zed itself will leave GitHub.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. Zed's own framing and marketing language (e.g. 'continuous engineering', 'race to replace GitHub') is consistently presented as attributed company framing rather than adopted as the article's own voice, including in the dedicated 'Framing' section which explicitly labels it as such.

Both sources fetched successfully, no suspicious patterns, every direct quote verified verbatim, no fabricated or misattributed specifics, sources array and body citations match bidirectionally, neutral tone, genuinely new topic.
